analysis:
Reviewed the head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1607-2422). The PR's only visible changed range is head line 1406: a new documentation table row for `demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens`, a paged complete-store effective-token floor for dense Qwen3.5/3.8 that ends a checkpoint range just below the prompt end. Both supplied units are unchanged surrounding documentation, with no code, permission, crypto or protocol changes. No trust boundary, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing control is altered by this doc-only edit.

The new row touches the prefix-cache area (T-041, TB-007). It only describes a checkpoint boundary policy for the encrypted SSD paged complete store. It does not loosen the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate, the 30-minute TTL, the HMAC lookup names (SSDLookupKeys) or the cacheSalt scoping. Because it is a doc row, the claim that a range ends just below the prompt end when it saves at least the floor is unverified. The implementing code (EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift) and any new at-rest artifact or per-donation gating effects are outside the supplied evidence, so the next pass should check them if present in other batches. Specifically: whether the extra end-of-prompt checkpoint donations keep the existing per-donation adoption/benefit gate and salt-folded HMAC tags, and whether the 'streamed complete checkpoints' section in prefix-cache.md is consistent with T-041.

The surrounding MTP, sampling, tool-parser, reasoning and MiMo documentation is pre-existing narrative; I found nothing in it indicating a new security regression.
